headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when OpenMetadata feeds a writable Replit Agent workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata exposes MCP/server-style outputs and webhooks, while Replit Agent reads and writes Repl workspace files and can use broad networked tool calls. That creates a plausible bridge where OpenMetadata content is copied into Replit and treated as instructions. The pairwise interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata outputs are copied into Replit workspace files or prompts, injection becomes reachable.
IF Replit Agent parses OpenMetadata-generated text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Require a human review step before any OpenMetadata text is pasted into Replit.
Prefix imported OpenMetadata content with a non-executable delimiter and schema.
Disable automatic ingestion of OpenMetadata webhooks into agent prompts.
Use separate workspaces for catalog output and agent instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging so Replit ignores untrusted OpenMetadata text as instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, and memory/tribal knowledge, while Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration and can write files and egress broadly. If OpenMetadata data is placed into the Repl workspace, Replit can read and potentially transmit it to external services. Because the pairwise bridge is plausible and the blast radius includes secrets or governance data, high is warranted.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata-managed metadata includes secrets, governance notes, or lineage records in the Repl workspace, Replit Agent can read them.
IF Replit Agent sends workspace contents to package registries or deployment APIs, those data can leave the workspace.
mitigations: Keep OpenMetadata exports out of the Repl workspace.
Store secrets only in Replit Secrets, never in catalog files.
Restrict Replit network egress during catalog import tasks.
Review any generated diffs for accidental metadata disclosure.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level DLP or redaction before agent access.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata supports multiple instances and MCP/API-driven collaboration, while Replit Agent has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad shell/network capabilities in a persistent Repl filesystem. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can race and corrupt state. The overlap is directly supported by both profiles, so high is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents target the same Repl filesystem or git repository, write conflicts are possible.
IF OpenMetadata-driven automation and Replit Agent edits run concurrently, last-writer-wins corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch or directory.
Pause one agent before the other writes to shared files.
Require git locks or a merge gate before commits.
Limit OpenMetadata to read-only export during Replit edits.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata can emit lineage, governance, and trust metadata that Replit Agent may use as context for code changes or deployments. Replit Agent has action-taking authority through shell, package installs, and deployment APIs, so unverified upstream metadata can cascade into incorrect edits or rollout decisions. The pathway exists, but there is no direct evidence that Replit blindly trusts OpenMetadata, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Replit Agent uses OpenMetadata output as authoritative input without verification, errors can propagate into code or deployment actions.
IF OpenMetadata lineage or trust metadata is stale, Replit may act on incorrect assumptions.
mitigations: Add a verification checklist before acting on OpenMetadata output.
Require a second source for any deployment-affecting metadata.
Mark OpenMetadata fields as advisory in prompts.
Review generated changes before execution.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between catalog metadata and repo state.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance and memory/tribal knowledge, while Replit Agent handles source code, secrets, and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl. If regulated data or internal secrets are copied from OpenMetadata into Replit, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated metadata or secrets are stored in Replit workspace files, Replit retention and access controls apply.
IF OpenMetadata records are subject to stricter governance than the Repl workspace, policy mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated records in the Repl workspace.
Confirm retention settings for both systems before syncing data.
Use synthetic or redacted metadata for testing.
Document which data classes may cross the boundary.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated fields.
